A_admissions_architecture.primary_application_route: Two entirely separate application systems, gated by LOCAL vs. NON-LOCAL status (not by qualification type). (1) JUPAS (Joint University Programmes Admissions System, jupas.edu.hk) is the shared national platform used by 9 JUPAS-participating institutions, but it is open only to local applicants holding (past and/or current) HKDSE Examination results who are not already enrolled full-time in a JUPAS bachelor's programme. (2) Non-JUPAS is not a single shared platform at all — it is a label for each institution's own separate direct-application scheme, run through that university's own online application portal (e.g. HKU's own International/Non-JUPAS system, CUHK's own Non-JUPAS/International system at admission.cuhk.edu.hk, HKUST's own system at join.hkust.edu.hk). As of the 2020 JUPAS cycle, in accordance with HKSAR Government policy, ALL non-local applicants — regardless of whether they hold HKDSE results — must apply via non-JUPAS at each university individually, not via JUPAS. Non-JUPAS also covers local applicants whose eligibility rests on combining HKDSE with another qualification, or who hold no HKDSE result at all.
A_admissions_architecture.centralized_or_decentralized: Bifurcated by applicant type, more sharply than any of the six countries in the existing package. For the LOCAL/HKDSE segment: centralized application (JUPAS platform, shared fee schedule, shared timeline) feeding a centralized-ish matching algorithm, but with admission ratings still set independently per programme. For the NON-LOCAL/international segment (which is where essentially every Turkish MEB/IB/A-Level applicant sits): fully decentralized — no shared platform, no shared timeline, no shared fee, no shared application form across the 9 institutions. A student applying to HKU, CUHK and HKUST as an international applicant is filing three unrelated applications.
major_application_platforms: JUPAS (jupas.edu.hk) — shared platform for local/HKDSE applicants across 9 participating institutions; NOT used by non-local applicants under any circumstance since the 2020 cycle

Each university's own non-JUPAS/International Admissions portal (HKU, CUHK, HKUST, PolyU, CityU, EdUHK, HKBU, LingnanU, and others each run their own) — the required route for essentially all non-local/international applicants, including Turkish MEB/IB/A-Level holders
A_admissions_architecture.direct_university_application_possible: For non-local/international applicants this is not merely possible, it is the ONLY route — there is no centralized alternative available to them at all. For local applicants the reverse is true in the ordinary case: JUPAS is required for anyone relying on HKDSE results alone, and direct/non-JUPAS application is reserved for local applicants combining HKDSE with another qualification or holding no HKDSE result.
A_admissions_architecture.application_limit_if_any: Within JUPAS: up to 20 programme choices, organized into 5 preference bands (Band A = choices 1-3, Band B = choices 4-6, and so on) — see application_strategy_constraints. Within non-JUPAS: no shared cross-university limit exists because there is no shared platform; each university sets its own internal choice count on its own application (this was not independently confirmed at a specific number for HKU/CUHK/HKUST in sources reviewed this pass and should not be assumed uniform).
A_admissions_architecture.parallel_application_rules: A non-local/international applicant wanting to be considered by multiple Hong Kong universities must submit a fully separate application, with a separate fee, separate documents, and separate deadline, to each institution individually — there is no JUPAS-style shared preference list across universities for this applicant type.
A_admissions_architecture.scope: national/government policy (the 2020 rule confining ALL non-local applicants to non-JUPAS) + platform (JUPAS's internal mechanics) + university (each non-JUPAS scheme's own portal, deadlines and criteria)

B_qualification_eligibility.recognition_mechanism: Two-layer pattern structurally similar to Netherlands' Nuffic/university split. (1) HKCAAVQ (Hong Kong Council for Accreditation of Academic and Vocational Qualifications), a statutory body, offers an individual 'Qualification Assessment' service giving a professional opinion on whether a given applicant's qualification meets a stated Hong Kong Qualifications Framework level; this assessment is specific to the individual applicant, is not itself a university admission decision, and is used for multiple purposes beyond university admission (professional registration, the Quality Migrant Admission Scheme, teacher registration). (2) Each university independently publishes its own qualification-specific, often country-specific, minimum-grade tables (built from its own equivalency research) and makes the actual binding admission decision; where an applicant's qualification is not on a university's pre-published list, HKU's own page states results 'will be considered on an individual basis' — a discretionary fallback rather than an automatic referral to HKCAAVQ.
B_qualification_eligibility.baseline_qualification_expectation: For local applicants: an HKDSE Examination result (or in some non-JUPAS local cases, HKALE/pre-2012 qualifications) is the baseline. For non-local/international applicants there is no single baseline credential — universities each publish an accepted-qualification list covering the IB Diploma, GCE A-Level/International A-Level, US high-school diploma plus SAT/AP, French Baccalauréat, and dozens of national qualifications (HKUST's list names 80+ countries/regions, explicitly including Turkey). A plain foreign secondary diploma alone is evaluated against that specific university's own published minimum (see the Türkiye section below for the clearest documented example of this varying by university).
B_qualification_eligibility.subject_prerequisites_general: Programme-specific rather than governed by one national profile system. STEM, engineering and quantitative-social-science programmes commonly require Mathematics at an advanced level (e.g. HKUST requires Mathematics at Advanced Level for its Math/STEM-track admission, and separately states Further Mathematics can be counted toward, but is not required for, the Mathematics requirement); IB-track applicants to competitive programmes are commonly expected to have taken 3 Higher Level subjects including a quantitative HL subject for STEM/business fields.
B_qualification_eligibility.equivalency_process: Each university maintains its own qualification-by-qualification, and in some cases country-by-country, minimum entry standard, published on its own international-qualifications admissions pages (a dynamic qualification/country selector tool at HKU and HKUST; a general-requirements PDF at CUHK). These are university artifacts, not a shared national table.
B_qualification_eligibility.university_discretion: Substantial, and concretely evidenced (not just structurally implied) — see the Türkiye section: HKU and CUHK publish two different minimum averages for the same named Turkish diploma types.

credentials_covered.turkiye_meb: Standard Turkish state/Anatolian high-school diplomas (named on Hong Kong university pages as 'Anadolu Lisesi / Devlet Lise Diplomasi / Lise Bitirme Diplomasi') are explicitly recognized qualification types at HKU and CUHK, each with its own published minimum average — see dedicated Türkiye section below.
credentials_covered.ib_diploma: Widely accepted as a standard non-local qualification. HKU cites a minimum IB Diploma score of 31; HKUST cites a minimum of 34-35 with a stated '37+' as competitive, and requires at least 3 Higher Level subjects for its more selective programmes.
credentials_covered.a_levels: GCE A-Level / International A-Level widely accepted. HKU cites a minimum of 2A and 1B; CUHK accepts '3AL passes or 2AL+2AS passes' with programme-specific subject requirements; HKUST requires Mathematics at Advanced Level for STEM-track admission.
credentials_covered.ap_plus_us_diploma: A US high-school diploma is accepted when combined with AP exam results and/or SAT scores; HKU cites a minimum redesigned SAT score of 1350 as one accepted evidentiary path.
credentials_covered.french_bac: Listed among HKUST's accepted qualification types (French-patterned systems); specific minimum grade thresholds were not confirmed in sources reviewed this pass.
credentials_covered.german_abitur: Not specifically confirmed with a published threshold in sources reviewed this pass; Germany is not among the countries whose specific figures were pulled in this research session — treat as a gap, not a confirmed absence.

turkiye_applicant_view.standard_diploma_sufficient_for_direct_e: Yes, but ONLY through the non-JUPAS/international route (JUPAS itself is categorically closed to Turkish/any non-local applicant, see A above) — and the required minimum is set independently, and differently, by each university. Two official, university-specific figures were directly confirmed for the same named diploma types ('Anadolu Lisesi / Devlet Lise Diplomasi / Lise Bitirme Diplomasi', i.e. the standard Turkish state/Anatolian MEB-administered high-school diploma): HKU requires 'an overall average of 4 on a 5-point scale or 70 on a 100-point scale' (admissions.hku.hk/node/2326, primary source, verbatim); CUHK requires an overall average of 80% (per its official cuhk.edu.hk international-qualifications guide; corroborated via multiple independent secondary references to that exact official PDF but not directly text-parsed by this research pass, so treated as secondary-corroborated rather than verbatim-verified). This is the same 'not one national fact' pattern documented for the Netherlands (Tilburg 85% vs. VU 80%+APs) — a Turkish applicant cannot assume one Hong Kong university's threshold applies at another. HKUST's specific Turkish-diploma threshold was not found in sources reviewed this pass — a genuine gap, not evidence that HKUST is more lenient or stricter.
turkiye_applicant_view.additional_qualifications_commonly_requi: No Hong Kong-specific supplementary-qualification pathway (comparable to the Netherlands' 'AP exams' or 'one year of Turkish Lisans credits' routes) was identified in sources reviewed this pass for applicants whose plain Lise diploma average falls short of a given university's threshold. HKU's own general policy — that a qualification not matching a published table 'will be considered on an individual basis' — implies some discretionary path exists, but no concrete Turkey-specific bridging mechanism was confirmed. Treat as unresolved, not as 'no such path exists.'
turkiye_applicant_view.ap_ib_a_level_impact: Not independently confirmed for the Turkey-to-Hong-Kong combination specifically in this research pass. By the general pattern seen across Hong Kong universities' qualification-by-qualification (not diploma-blended) evaluation model, a student holding a full IB Diploma or A-Levels rather than a plain Turkish Lise diploma would likely be assessed against the IB or A-Level tables instead of the Lise-diploma table — this mirrors the Netherlands finding directionally — but this is an inference from structural pattern, not a verified Hong Kong-specific finding, and should be flagged to the student as such rather than asserted.
turkiye_applicant_view.national_entrance_exam_relevance: No source reviewed addressed whether a Turkish applicant's YKS (national university entrance exam) result plays any role in a Hong Kong university's assessment of a Lise diploma holder. This mirrors the exact same unresolved gap documented in the Netherlands research — treat as a genuine unknown, not as confirmed irrelevance.
turkiye_applicant_view.foundation_year_common: No Hong Kong-specific foundation-year or bridge-year mechanism for Turkish (or other non-local) applicants whose secondary qualification falls short of a university's threshold was identified in sources reviewed this pass. This is a gap, not a confirmed absence — do not assume no such pathway exists.
turkiye_applicant_view.recognition_centralized_or_university_sp: University-specific in the outcome that matters to the student, exactly as in the Netherlands. There is no Hong Kong-wide binding Turkish-diploma threshold; HKCAAVQ can provide an individual qualification opinion, but the two admission-determining figures actually found (HKU's 4/5 or 70/100; CUHK's 80%) come from each university's own published table, not from HKCAAVQ or any government body.

academic_evidence_used.transcript_role: For non-JUPAS/international applicants, a full academic transcript is a required upload at every university reviewed (explicitly listed among HKU Business School's required non-JUPAS documents: 'Academic transcript(s) issued by your high school / institution, showing your grades/examination results'). For JUPAS/local applicants, the operative academic evidence is the HKDSE Statement/Certificate of Results itself rather than a running school transcript.
academic_evidence_used.native_grades_handling: Not force-converted to one universal GPA. For JUPAS/local applicants, HKDSE subject levels are converted onto a shared 7-point scale (5**=7 down to U=0) used consistently by HKU, CUHK, HKUST, PolyU and CityU as the JUPAS baseline conversion — but this conversion is internal to the HKDSE scale itself, not a cross-qualification universal GPA. For non-JUPAS/international applicants, each university reads the qualification on its own native scale and applies its own published qualification-specific minimum (IB point score out of 45; A-Level letter grades; Turkish 100-point or 5-point average) rather than forcing everything into one figure.
academic_evidence_used.predicted_grades_role: No native predicted-grade concept for the HKDSE/JUPAS track — see dedicated predicted_grades section below. For non-JUPAS/international applicants using curricula that natively produce predictions (IB, A-Level), predicted grades are an explicitly named, actively used document category (HKU Business School: 'Predicted grades/scores for your upcoming examination issued by your school (if applicable)') feeding conditional-offer decisions.
academic_evidence_used.final_grades_role: Required to convert any conditional offer to unconditional/final in both tracks. For JUPAS, the defining mechanic is that the Main Round offer itself is issued only after HKDSE results are released (see admissions_decision_model) — so, unlike the UK, the ordinary JUPAS applicant is not working from a predicted-grade-based conditional offer at the point of the main decision.
academic_evidence_used.external_exams_role: The HKDSE itself is simultaneously the local school-leaving credential AND a centrally, externally graded standardized examination administered by HKEAA (Hong Kong Examinations and Assessment Authority) — a dual role that has no exact analogue among the Netherlands/Germany/Italy patterns already documented, where the school-leaving diploma and any 'standardized test' are more separable concepts. For non-local applicants, whatever external exam board graded their own qualification (IB, Cambridge/Pearson for A-Level, College Board for AP/SAT) is simply read as that qualification's own native evidence.
academic_evidence_used.course_rigor_signal: Read through programme-specific subject requirements (see subject_prerequisites) rather than a codified national profile system comparable to Dutch VWO's profielen.
academic_evidence_used.standardized_tests: No universal national admissions test for either track. See dedicated standardized_tests section for the HKDSE's own hybrid role and SAT's narrow supplementary use.

predicted_grades.are_used: Not as a native HKDSE/JUPAS concept. The defining mechanic of JUPAS's Main Round is that it runs on ACTUAL, final HKDSE results, not forward-looking predictions — structurally closer to Germany's final-Abitur-result model than to the UK's predicted-grade-driven UCAS mechanic. (A narrower School Principal's Nomination (SPN) pathway can involve pre-results consideration, but this was not deeply verified this pass and should not be read as the general JUPAS mechanism.)
predicted_grades.where: Predicted grades ARE used, but only for non-JUPAS/international applicants whose own curriculum natively produces them (IB predicted points by subject/level; UK-style A-Level predicted grades) — read operationally by Hong Kong universities to make an admission decision before final results are known, exactly as in the Netherlands' treatment of foreign predicted grades.
predicted_grades.by_whom: Issued by the applicant's own school/teachers under IB/exam-board rules — not generated, estimated, or verified by any Hong Kong body. For HKDSE/JUPAS applicants: not applicable, no equivalent document exists.
predicted_grades.for_what: To allow non-JUPAS decisions (and conditional offers) to be made before an IB/A-Level applicant's final results are published — necessary because non-JUPAS deadlines and decision timelines (e.g. CUHK/HKUST regular-round deadlines around 8 January) run many months ahead of IB/A-Level final results (typically July), independent of HKDSE's own July results timeline.
predicted_grades.conditional_offer_relationship: Directly linked. HKU's own guidance states it 'may extend conditional offers to non-JUPAS candidates who have entered for examinations with a view to satisfying entrance requirements by August, conditional upon obtaining necessary examination results' — the predicted-grade-based non-JUPAS offer becomes unconditional once actual final results are produced.
predicted_grades.final_result_requirement: Yes for both tracks — a non-JUPAS conditional offer requires final qualifying results before enrolment; a JUPAS Main Round offer is, for most applicants, already based on final HKDSE results by construction.

conditional_vs_unconditional_admission.concept_exists: Yes, but the two tracks use it in structurally different ways — a genuine, non-obvious finding.
conditional_vs_unconditional_admission.explanation: For JUPAS/local applicants: the ordinary Main Round offer is issued AFTER HKDSE results are released, so for the large majority of JUPAS applicants there is no meaningful predicted-grade-conditional stage at the point of the primary decision — the mechanic is closer to 'final results in, offer out' than to a conditional-then-confirmed model. A narrower pre-results conditional-offer mechanism exists and was referenced in relation to nominated (SPN) applicants specifically, but its scope was not fully verified this pass. For non-JUPAS/international applicants (essentially all Turkish MEB/IB/A-Level applicants): conditional offers are the norm for anyone applying before final results are available, explicitly confirmed at HKU ('conditional offers... conditional upon obtaining necessary examination results') and structurally implied by CUHK/HKUST's own January decision timelines running well ahead of July IB/A-Level results.

subject_prerequisites.pattern: Programme-specific rather than governed by one codified national subject-profile system (contrast with Dutch VWO's four fixed profielen). STEM, engineering, and quantitative business/economics programmes commonly publish a Mathematics-at-advanced-level requirement (e.g. HKUST requires Mathematics at Advanced Level for its STEM-track admission and treats Further Mathematics as acceptable toward, though not a substitute for, the core Mathematics requirement); IB-track applicants to competitive quantitative programmes are commonly expected to present Higher Level Mathematics among their 3 required HL subjects.
subject_prerequisites.scope: programme (individual Bachelor's programmes and schools set their own required subjects; there is no single national subject-profile taxonomy comparable to VWO's profielen for Hong Kong to map foreign curricula onto)
illustrative_examples: HKUST STEM/Engineering programmes: Mathematics at Advanced Level (A-Level) required; Further Mathematics accepted as contributing toward, but not replacing, this requirement.
IB-track applicants to competitive quantitative programmes (Business, Engineering, Economics-adjacent fields) commonly expected to present 3 Higher Level subjects including a quantitative HL subject.

Medicine programmes (non-JUPAS route) commonly expect Biology/Chemistry-equivalent prior coursework alongside the general academic threshold, though a fully codified national subject table (comparable to Dutch vakkeneisen) was not found in sources reviewed.
subject_prerequisites.vwo_profielen_detail: Not applicable — Hong Kong has no direct analogue to the Dutch VWO profiel system. HKDSE students themselves choose 4 compulsory core subjects (Chinese Language, English Language, Mathematics, Citizenship and Social Development) plus 1-4 elective subjects from a bank of roughly 20 electives, but this is a flexible subject-selection structure, not a fixed small set of named profiles universities can key requirements off of the way Dutch programmes key off C&M/E&M/N&G/N&T.

standardized_tests.mandatory_optional_status: Not mandatory nationally in the SAT/ACT sense for either track. For local/JUPAS applicants, the HKDSE itself already functions as Hong Kong's own centrally-administered, externally-graded standardized examination — a dual role (school-leaving credential + standardized test) that makes a separate universal admissions test unnecessary for this track. For non-JUPAS/international applicants, SAT/AP scores surface mainly as supplementary or qualification-specific evidence for applicants presenting a US high-school-diploma pathway (HKU cites a minimum redesigned SAT of 1350 as one accepted evidentiary route), not as a requirement imposed on IB, A-Level, or other qualification types.
standardized_tests.current_cycle_note: No evidence found of a general SAT/ACT requirement being introduced for the 2026-2027 cycle; treat SAT/ACT-as-a-universal-requirement as a confirmed non-feature of the Hong Kong system based on sources reviewed. Separately, TOEFL iBT itself is undergoing a scoring-scale change (a new score-reporting scale applies to tests taken from 21 January 2026 onward per HKU/HKUST English-requirement pages) — a real, time-sensitive, English-test-specific change, not a Hong-Kong-specific academic-test change.
programme_specific_tests: No Hong Kong-specific bespoke aptitude/reasoning test comparable to TU Delft's Mathematics + Systematic Reasoning test (Netherlands) or UK's UCAT/LNAT/TMUA was identified in sources reviewed this pass for HKU/CUHK/HKUST undergraduate Medicine, Law, or Business admission — these programmes appear to rely on academic threshold plus interview rather than a separate written admissions test, but this was not exhaustively verified and should not be treated as a confirmed absence.

language_requirements.framework: Two distinct evidentiary paths depending on track. For local/JUPAS applicants: HKDSE's own English Language subject result is commonly treated as sufficient English evidence by Hong Kong universities themselves (all HK undergraduate programmes are predominantly English-medium outside Chinese-specific programmes), and a benchmarking study conducted jointly by HKEAA and the British Council maps HKDSE English Level 5 to roughly IELTS 7.0, Level 5* to roughly IELTS 7.5, and Level 4 to roughly IELTS 6.5 — used informally by universities/agencies as a reference point, explicitly NOT described as an official automatic conversion. For non-JUPAS/international applicants: a separate English-proficiency test is required unless exempted (first-language English, or prior education substantially conducted in English) — commonly IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, or similar.
language_requirements.exemption_pattern: Exemptions are granted at university/programme level for applicants whose prior education was substantially in English or who are nationals of English-primary-language countries — mirroring the Netherlands' exemption logic. HKUST states explicitly that TOEFL/IELTS is not required 'if their first language is English, or they obtained the bachelor's degree from an institution where the medium of instruction was English.'
language_requirements.where_variation_begins: At the university level, and inconsistently even within a single university's own pages. HKU's general international-qualifications English-requirement page states a baseline of IELTS 6.0 overall (no subtest below 5.5) or TOEFL iBT 80 (transitioning to a new TOEFL score scale from 21 January 2026); HKUST states an equivalent TOEFL iBT 80 / IELTS 6.0 baseline. However, HKU's own Turkey-specific qualification page (admissions.hku.hk/node/2326) states a materially higher threshold — IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 93 — for that specific qualification pathway. This is a genuine inconsistency across HKU's own published pages, not a resolved single figure; ORYN should verify the specific, currently-live page for the applicant's exact qualification/programme combination rather than treating either number as universally authoritative. CUHK separately excludes IELTS One Skill Retake, IELTS Indicator, and IELTS Online score reports as valid evidence.

application_timing.cycle: 2026-2027 academic year (entry September 2026); structural pattern expected to repeat for 2027-28 but specific dates should be re-verified closer to that cycle.
application_timing.major_deadline_pattern: JUPAS (local/HKDSE track): a single, nationally-synchronized cycle. Standard application period 9 October 2025 (9:00am) to 3 December 2025 (5:00pm); a late application period runs 5 December 2025 (9:00am) to 27 May 2026 (5:00pm) at a higher fee. The Main Round offer is issued after HKDSE results are released; the exact 2026 HKDSE results-release date was not confirmed from a primary HKEAA source in this research pass (HKEAA's own site returned repeated access errors to automated fetch this session) and should be treated as an unresolved specific date, though the sequencing itself — results first, then Main Round offers — is confirmed.
application_timing.numerus_fixus_deadline: Not applicable in the Dutch numerus-fixus sense (a materially earlier deadline for capped programmes within the same platform) — JUPAS runs one shared timeline for all programmes, including Medicine and other capacity-limited fields; the capacity constraint operates through the merit-order/rating mechanism at decision time, not through an earlier submission deadline.

constraints: JUPAS: up to 20 programme choices, grouped into 5 preference bands (Band A = choices 1-3, Band B = choices 4-6, Band C = choices 7-9, and so on). Institutions see only which band a given applicant placed their programme in, not the applicant's exact rank order, until after Main Round results are announced — a deliberate anti-gaming design distinct from anything documented in the other 6 countries. Per JUPAS's own statistics, most offers come from Band A choices, making the first 3 choices and their internal order the most consequential decision an applicant makes.

The JUPAS Main Round produces exactly ONE offer per applicant — the highest-priority choice on the applicant's list for which their position in that programme's own merit-order list clears the cutoff — via a computer-run 'iteration process' that matches applicant preference order against each programme's independently-set merit-order ranking. This is neither a UK-style firm/insurance dual-offer mechanic nor a simple sequential ranked list processed one choice at a time; it is closer to a simultaneous, blinded matching/clearing algorithm.

Non-JUPAS has no equivalent shared choice-limit concept, because there is no shared platform: an international applicant applies separately, and pays a separate fee, to each Hong Kong university individually (CUHK's non-JUPAS application fee: HK$500; JUPAS's own fee, for comparison and not paid by non-local applicants, is HK$460 standard / HK$810 late).
Non-JUPAS deadlines are university-specific and NOT synchronized with each other or with JUPAS — see application_timing.
application_strategy_constraints.explanation: The band mechanism exists specifically to let JUPAS institutions rank applicants fairly without knowing (and thus without being able to game around) each applicant's precise ordering of competing offers — a materially different anti-gaming design from UCAS's firm/insurance model, which instead relies on the applicant making a binding choice after all offers are in hand.

personal_statement_essays.role: Not identified as a requirement of JUPAS's core local/HKDSE pathway in sources reviewed this pass (consistent with the pathway being driven primarily by the HKDSE score and programme-set rating criteria) — though a narrower SPN (School Principal's Nomination) mechanism may involve additional holistic material and was not deeply verified this pass. For non-JUPAS/international applicants, a personal statement is commonly part of the application: HKU Business School explicitly lists 'personal statement' among the materials its admission decisions rely on.
personal_statement_essays.explanation: Where present, this is a non-JUPAS/university-specific and, within that, programme-specific requirement rather than a Hong-Kong-wide universal feature — the same 'programme-scoped, not universal' pattern documented for the Netherlands' numerus fixus motivation letter.

recommendation_letters.role: Inconsistent treatment even within sources reviewed, which is itself the finding worth recording rather than picking one figure. HKU Business School's own non-JUPAS document list marks its reference/recommendation letter as explicitly '(optional)', sourced from a school principal, teacher, or academic/personal referee. A separate general description of HKUST's non-JUPAS document set (secondary source) names 'recommendation letters' among required documents without the word optional. No source reviewed described recommendation letters as a factor in the standard local JUPAS pathway.
recommendation_letters.explanation: Do not assume a single Hong Kong-wide answer to 'are recommendation letters required.' Treat this as genuinely varying by university and possibly by programme, and verify the current, specific programme's own document checklist rather than generalizing from one faculty's page.

extracurricular_activities.role: Not documented as a primary factor in JUPAS's core Best-5-score/merit-order mechanism for the ordinary local applicant. A named School Principal's Nomination (SPN) pathway exists within JUPAS that appears related to non-purely-academic or principal-endorsed factors, but its precise mechanism and weight were not deeply verified in this research pass and should not be assumed to mean extracurriculars are broadly weighted within standard JUPAS scoring.
extracurricular_activities.nuance: For non-JUPAS/international applicants, a CV/resume is explicitly OPTIONAL at HKU Business School (capped at two A4 pages, covering 'activities, achievements, work experience') — suggesting extracurricular evidence can be submitted as supporting context but is not established as an independently-weighted primary admissions category the way it can be in US holistic review. This is directionally similar to, but less firmly evidenced than, the Netherlands' 'motivation-letter-only, not independently weighted' finding.

interviews_tests_portfolios.pattern: Interviews are confirmed, programme-specific, and concentrated in competitive professional programmes for the non-JUPAS/international pathway specifically: HKU Medicine (Multiple Mini Interview / MMI format; interviewers may switch to Chinese to test proficiency), CUHK Medicine (panel format), HKU Law (interviews conducted, including via Zoom), HKU Business (optional, shortlisted-applicants-only, individual Skype/Zoom format). HKUST states explicitly that interviews are 'not a compulsory part of the Non-JUPAS application process' generally and are 'conducted at the discretion of individual programmes.' No confirmed portfolio requirement for Art/Design/Architecture-type programmes was found in sources reviewed this pass — a genuine gap, not evidence that no such requirement exists.
interviews_tests_portfolios.when_applicable: Concentrated in high-demand professional/competitive fields (Medicine, Law, and at some institutions Business) rather than a universal feature of either JUPAS or non-JUPAS application; standard non-selective programmes were not documented as requiring interviews.

restricted_selective_programmes.numerus_fixus_explanation: Two distinct, stacked capacity constraints exist, and they should not be conflated. (1) System-wide: the Hong Kong government caps UGC-funded first-year-first-degree places at approximately 15,000 per year, reserved for local students (the JUPAS-eligible pool); roughly 80% of these funded places are filled via JUPAS itself, with the remainder (roughly 600 places) filled via non-JUPAS routes serving mainland Gaokao candidates, associate-degree graduates, and other local-but-non-JUPAS categories. (2) Separately, a government-set ceiling on NON-LOCAL student enrolment exists as a percentage of the local student number — raised from 20% to 40% for the 2024/25 academic year, and further to 50% from the 2026-27 academic year — but this quota is layered ADDITIONALLY on top of, not carved out of, the protected 15,000 local funded places; non-local students under this quota are self-funded, not publicly funded. (3) Within both pools, individual programmes (most visibly Medicine) additionally set their own hard capacity ceilings and run competitive selection within that ceiling — CUHK's Medicine programme, for example, offers 300 places for HKDSE-track/high-school-graduate entry plus 25 places for degree-holder (advanced-standing) entry from 2025 entry onward, and does not publish a separate fixed JUPAS-vs-non-JUPAS sub-quota, instead describing non-JUPAS Medicine applicants as evaluated against a 'top 1-2% HKDSE-equivalent' standard.
restricted_selective_programmes.current_mechanism: For JUPAS/local applicants: capacity constraint operates through the merit-order rating and iteration/matching process itself (see application_strategy_constraints) rather than through a separate lottery or lower registration cap — meeting a baseline threshold does not itself guarantee a place in a capacity-constrained programme like Medicine, since the programme's own merit-order cutoff for that cycle determines actual admission. For non-JUPAS/international applicants to the same capacity-constrained programmes: competitive holistic review against the university's published minimum plus, commonly, an interview (see interviews_tests_portfolios) — CUHK's own description of evaluating non-JUPAS Medicine applicants against a 'top 1-2%' standard indicates this is a genuinely competitive, not threshold-only, process for this pathway too.
example_fields: Medicine (MBChB) — the clearest documented example; CUHK cites 300 HKDSE-track + 25 advanced-standing places from 2025 entry
Law (LLB) — HKU Law conducts interviews for non-JUPAS applicants, indicating selective treatment, though specific seat counts were not confirmed this pass
Business/Business Administration at HKU — optional interview for shortlisted non-JUPAS applicants, indicating some selectivity beyond a pure grade threshold

Dentistry — referenced by pattern in general Hong Kong higher-education commentary as a capacity-constrained clinical-placement field, but specific seat counts were not independently confirmed in this research pass

admissions_decision_model.dominant_model: Genuinely bifurcated by applicant type first, and only secondarily by programme selectivity — a sharper and more fundamental split than in any of the six countries already documented, because the split happens at the level of 'which system can this applicant even use' rather than 'is this specific programme capped.'
admissions_decision_model.explanation: For LOCAL/JUPAS applicants: a merit-order/rating-and-matching model. Every programme, not just capacity-constrained ones like Medicine, sets its own rating of eligible applicants and has a hard place count; JUPAS's iteration process matches applicant preference order against each programme's merit-order list, producing exactly one offer per applicant at their highest-priority choice where they cleared that programme's cutoff for that cycle. This is closer to a simultaneous clearing/matching mechanism than either a Dutch-style binary threshold-equals-admission model (which applies to the Netherlands' large non-numerus-fixus majority) or a UK-style firm/insurance dual-offer model. For NON-LOCAL/international (non-JUPAS) applicants — which is where the great majority of Turkish MEB/IB/A-Level applicants sit — the model is university-specific holistic review: meeting a published qualification-specific minimum establishes eligibility to be considered, not a guarantee of admission (HKU and HKUST both state explicitly that meeting the stated minimum does not guarantee a place, since admission is 'competitive in nature'), and the final decision weighs transcript, predicted/final grades, and (variably by programme) personal statement, references, and interview performance.

safe_inferences: It is safe to infer that JUPAS is categorically unavailable to a Turkish MEB/IB/A-Level-educated applicant (or any non-local applicant) regardless of their HKDSE status — this is the single most important structural fact for ORYN to encode, confirmed directly and repeatedly on jupas.edu.hk and admissions.hku.hk.

It is safe to infer that non-JUPAS is not a shared platform — an applicant targeting multiple Hong Kong universities must plan for, budget for, and track fully separate applications, fees, and deadlines at each institution.

It is safe to infer that the same named Turkish diploma type can carry different minimum-grade thresholds at different Hong Kong universities (confirmed concretely: HKU's 4/5-or-70/100 vs. CUHK's 80% for the same 'Anadolu Lisesi / Devlet Lise Diplomasi / Lise Bitirme Diplomasi' credential) — a Turkish applicant should never assume one university's published threshold applies at another.

It is safe to infer that predicted grades matter operationally for non-JUPAS applicants using IB/A-Level (they are an explicitly named required-if-applicable document feeding conditional-offer decisions), even though the HKDSE/JUPAS track itself has no native predicted-grade concept and instead waits for final results before making its Main Round offer.

It is safe to infer that meeting a university's published minimum grade for a given qualification does not guarantee admission at either HKU or HKUST — both state this explicitly, and non-JUPAS is described by multiple institutions as competitive in nature.

It is safe to infer that financial proof (commonly cited around HKD 100,000-150,000) is a student-VISA/immigration requirement enforced by the HKSAR Immigration Department after an offer is made, not a factor the admissions committee weighs when deciding whether to make the offer — ORYN should not present financial proof as an admissions criterion.

It is safe to infer that interviews for non-JUPAS/international applicants concentrate in specific competitive professional programmes (Medicine, Law, and at some institutions Business) rather than applying universally.
unsafe_inferences: It is unsafe to assume JUPAS's existence means Hong Kong has a UK/UCAS-style single national application system for all applicants — JUPAS explicitly excludes all non-local applicants, which includes essentially every internationally-educated Turkish applicant.

It is unsafe to describe JUPAS's band-and-iteration mechanism as either a simple ranked list or a UK-style firm/insurance dual-offer system — it is a distinct, blinded, simultaneous matching mechanism where institutions cannot see an applicant's exact preference order until after results are announced.

It is unsafe to assume a Hong Kong university's general (non-qualification-specific) published English-language threshold is the one that applies to every applicant type — HKU's own general baseline (IELTS 6.0/TOEFL 80) and its Turkey-specific page (IELTS 6.5/TOEFL 93) genuinely disagree, and the currently-live, qualification-specific page should be checked at time of use.

It is unsafe to assume the HKDSE English Language Level-to-IELTS correspondence (e.g. 'Level 5 ≈ IELTS 7.0') functions as an automatic, guaranteed exemption — the benchmarking study itself is explicitly described as a reference correlation, not an official conversion, and competitive programmes/universities may still require a separate test.

It is unsafe to assume recommendation letters are either uniformly required or uniformly optional across Hong Kong non-JUPAS applications — sources reviewed disagree even at the level of a single university's different faculties.

It is unsafe to assume a bridge-year, foundation-year, or AP-style supplementary pathway exists for a Turkish applicant whose Lise average falls short of a given university's threshold — no such Hong Kong-specific mechanism was confirmed, and its absence from sources reviewed should be treated as an open gap, not proof that no such route exists.

It is unsafe to assume the non-local student quota (40% rising to 50%) is a scarcity constraint reducing local students' funded places — official sources are explicit that the 15,000 local UGC-funded places are protected and unreduced, and non-local admission is additional, self-funded capacity.

eligibility_competitiveness_fit.eligibility: Two categorically different gates depending on applicant type. For local applicants: holding valid local status plus an HKDSE result (or an approved alternative local qualification via non-JUPAS). For non-local/international applicants (essentially all Turkish MEB/IB/A-Level applicants): holding a qualification type the target university has published a policy for (or requesting individual consideration where it hasn't), typically expressed as a minimum average/points/grade combination that is university-specific and sometimes qualification-and-country-specific.
eligibility_competitiveness_fit.competitiveness: Genuinely present, and not merely a numerus-fixus-style exception layered on an otherwise-threshold system the way it is in the Netherlands. For JUPAS/local applicants, EVERY programme (not only Medicine-type fields) runs a merit-order rating and has a hard place count, so meeting a nominal minimum does not equal admission — competitiveness is closer to the UK/US end of the spectrum for this track. For non-JUPAS/international applicants, HKU and HKUST both state explicitly that meeting the published minimum does not guarantee admission and describe the process as competitive; CUHK's non-JUPAS Medicine standard ('top 1-2% HKDSE-equivalent') makes this concrete for one competitive field.
eligibility_competitiveness_fit.fit: For JUPAS/local applicants, fit is expressed mainly through the programme's own rating criteria (grades in relevant subjects, sometimes weighted) rather than a holistic narrative. For non-JUPAS/international applicants, fit assessment varies materially by university and programme — from a largely threshold-plus-transcript process at less competitive programmes to a personal-statement/reference/interview-inclusive holistic process at Medicine, Law, and Business specifically.

counselor_actions: Confirm immediately, before any other planning, that the student is a non-local applicant for Hong Kong purposes (requires a student visa, or is otherwise not a Hong Kong local/permanent resident) — this determines that JUPAS is entirely unavailable and non-JUPAS/international routes at each target university are the only path, regardless of whether the student later sits or has sat the HKDSE.

Because non-JUPAS is not a shared platform, help the student build a separate application checklist, fee budget, and deadline tracker per target Hong Kong university (HKU, CUHK, HKUST each run independent systems with independent timelines) rather than assuming one JUPAS-style unified process.

For a Turkish MEB-diploma-only student, check the SPECIFIC target university's own published Turkish-diploma threshold rather than assuming a single Hong Kong-wide figure — the confirmed HKU (4/5 or 70/100) vs. CUHK (80%) contrast shows this varies meaningfully, and HKUST's specific figure was not found and should be requested directly from HKUST admissions.

For a student holding IB or A-Levels (with or without Turkish schooling in their background), request predicted grades from the school early, since Hong Kong non-JUPAS decisions and conditional offers for this qualification type are explicitly built around predicted-grade submission ahead of final results.

For target programmes in Medicine, Law, or Business specifically, prepare the student for an interview as a likely (though not universally confirmed) requirement of the non-JUPAS process, and verify current-cycle interview format (MMI vs. panel vs. optional/shortlisted-only) directly with that specific school, since this varies by university and even by faculty within a university.

Do not treat meeting a published minimum grade threshold as equivalent to admission for either track — both JUPAS (via merit-order competition within programme capacity) and non-JUPAS (explicitly stated as competitive by HKU/HKUST) require clearing a further competitive bar beyond the minimum.

Separate financial-proof planning (a visa/immigration requirement, commonly cited around HKD 100,000-150,000) from admissions planning — it does not affect whether an offer is made, only whether the visa needed to act on an existing offer can be obtained.

Verify the specific, currently-live English-language-requirement page for the student's exact target qualification and programme rather than relying on a single university-wide figure — HKU's own pages showed inconsistent numbers (general baseline vs. Turkey-specific page) within this research pass alone.

Where no confirmed information exists (HKUST's Turkish-diploma threshold; a Hong Kong-specific bridge/foundation-year mechanism; YKS's relevance, if any) — tell the student and family this is unresolved and needs direct confirmation from the university's own admissions office, rather than presenting an inferred or estimated figure as fact.

data_model_implications.notes: Hong Kong requires ORYN's data model to represent, as a FIRST-CLASS distinction preceding any qualification-level logic, which of two entirely separate admission systems an applicant belongs to (local/JUPAS-eligible vs. non-local/non-JUPAS-only) — this is a coarser and more consequential split than the national/platform/university/programme layering alone captures, because it changes which platform, timeline, fee structure, and decision mechanism apply before any qualification-specific rule is even reached. Within the non-JUPAS branch (the one essentially all Turkish/internationally-educated applicants fall into), the model then needs the familiar four layers: (1) national/government policy (the 2020 all-non-local-applicants-use-non-JUPAS rule; the 15,000-local-place funding floor; the 40%→50% non-local quota ceiling), (2) platform (JUPAS's internal band/iteration mechanics — NOT applicable to the non-JUPAS branch at all, which has no shared platform layer), (3) university (each institution's own qualification-by-qualification, sometimes country-specific, minimum-grade tables — the Turkish-diploma HKU-vs-CUHK contrast is the clearest evidence), and (4) programme (Medicine/Law/Business-specific interview requirements and, for Medicine, its own hard capacity ceiling within the university). A single 'Hong Kong requirement' record per qualification type would be actively misleading, and a model that only distinguishes national/platform/university/programme without first gating on local-vs-non-local status would misroute every Turkish/international applicant into a system (JUPAS) they cannot actually use.
gaps: HKUST's specific published minimum-grade threshold for Turkish Lise-type diplomas was not found in sources reviewed this pass.

The exact 2026 HKDSE results-release date, and HKU's own specific non-JUPAS first-round deadline date for 2026 entry, were not confirmed from a primary source this pass (HKEAA's site returned repeated access errors to automated fetch, and HKU's PDF calendar was not machine-readable in this session).

The precise mechanism and evidentiary weight of JUPAS's School Principal's Nomination (SPN) pathway was named in sources but not deeply verified — it may be a meaningful non-purely-academic/extracurricular channel within JUPAS and deserves a dedicated follow-up pass.

Whether an IB/A-Level qualification layered on top of Turkish secondary schooling changes which evaluation table a Hong Kong university applies (as it demonstrably does in the Netherlands) was not independently confirmed for Hong Kong specifically.
Portfolio requirements for Art/Design/Architecture-type undergraduate programmes in Hong Kong were not confirmed in sources reviewed this pass.
Full non-JUPAS seat counts for Medicine at HKU and HKUST specifically (only CUHK's figures were confirmed with specific numbers), and for Law/Dentistry at any institution, were not confirmed.

system_university_programme_override_mod.explanation: Layer 0 (applicant-type gate, Hong Kong-specific and prior to the usual four layers): whether an applicant is 'local' or 'non-local' under HKSAR Government policy determines which entire system — JUPAS or non-JUPAS — is even available; this is set by government policy (the 2020 rule) and cannot be chosen or waived by either the applicant or the university. Layer 1 (national/government): the 15,000-place local funding floor and the 40%-rising-to-50% non-local quota ceiling are set in government/UGC policy and apply system-wide, uniform regardless of which university a student targets. Layer 2 (national credential-recognition baseline): HKCAAVQ can issue an individual qualification-assessment opinion referencing the Hong Kong Qualifications Framework, functioning similarly to Nuffic's role in the Netherlands as a system-level reference point that does not itself bind any university's decision. Layer 3 (university): each institution — for non-JUPAS applicants specifically, since JUPAS's own internal rating criteria are the platform-layer mechanic for local applicants — sets its own binding minimum-grade table per qualification type and, in some cases, per country (the HKU-70/100-vs-CUHK-80%-for-the-same-Turkish-diploma-type contrast is the clearest confirmed evidence of this). Layer 4 (programme): within a university, individual programmes layer on their own subject prerequisites, interview requirements (concentrated in Medicine/Law/Business), and — for capacity-constrained fields like Medicine — their own hard place count and merit-order/competitive standard (CUHK's 'top 1-2% HKDSE-equivalent' description for non-JUPAS Medicine). ORYN should never present a Layer 3 or Layer 4 fact (a specific university's Turkish-diploma threshold, or a specific programme's interview requirement) as if it were a Layer 0 or Layer 1 national fact — and, uniquely to Hong Kong among the countries researched so far, should never assume a Layer 1/Layer 2 platform mechanic (JUPAS itself) is even reachable without first confirming the applicant clears the Layer 0 local/non-local gate.

matrix_row.main_application_architecture: Bifurcated by applicant type before anything else: centralized platform + merit-order matching for local/HKDSE applicants (JUPAS); fully decentralized, direct-to-each-university applications for all non-local/international applicants (non-JUPAS) — which is where essentially all Turkish MEB/IB/A-Level applicants sit
matrix_row.central_platform: JUPAS (jupas.edu.hk) — but categorically unavailable to non-local applicants since the 2020 cycle; non-JUPAS has no equivalent shared platform at all, only separate per-university portals
matrix_row.direct_applications_possible: Not optional but mandatory and exclusive for non-local/international applicants (no centralized alternative exists for them); for local HKDSE-only applicants, JUPAS is instead the required route and direct/non-JUPAS application is the exception (combined qualifications or no HKDSE)
matrix_row.application_choice_limits: JUPAS: up to 20 programme choices in 5 preference bands (A=1-3, B=4-6, etc.), producing exactly one offer via a blinded matching algorithm; non-JUPAS: no shared limit concept — each university application is separate, with its own fee (e.g. CUHK HK$500) and no cross-university coordination
matrix_row.predicted_grades_role: No native concept for HKDSE/JUPAS, whose Main Round offer is issued only after final HKDSE results are released; predicted grades ARE used operationally for non-JUPAS/international applicants presenting IB or A-Level, feeding explicit conditional offers ahead of final results
matrix_row.subject_prerequisites: Programme-specific (e.g. Mathematics at Advanced Level for HKUST STEM programmes; HL Mathematics commonly expected for competitive IB-track quantitative programmes) rather than governed by one codified national subject-profile system
matrix_row.standardized_tests: No universal national admissions test; the HKDSE itself doubles as Hong Kong's own centrally-graded standardized exam for local applicants; SAT/AP appear only as supplementary qualification-specific evidence for US-diploma-pathway non-JUPAS applicants (HKU cites a minimum redesigned SAT of 1350)
matrix_row.language_proof: For local applicants, HKDSE's own English Language result is commonly treated as sufficient (informally benchmarked, not an official automatic conversion, to roughly IELTS 6.5-7.5 depending on level); for non-JUPAS/international applicants, separate IELTS/TOEFL required unless exempted — general baseline commonly IELTS 6.0/TOEFL 80, though this varies by university page (HKU's own Turkey-specific page cites a higher IELTS 6.5/TOEFL 93)
matrix_row.essays_motivation: Not documented as part of JUPAS's core local pathway; a personal statement is commonly part of non-JUPAS/international applications at the university/programme level (e.g. explicitly named at HKU Business School)
matrix_row.recommendations: Inconsistent across sources even within one university — optional at HKU Business School specifically, described as part of the general required document set for HKUST non-JUPAS in secondary sources; not documented for the standard local JUPAS pathway
matrix_row.extracurricular_role: Not documented as a primary factor in JUPAS's core merit-order mechanism; for non-JUPAS, an optional CV/resume (HKU Business School, 2-page cap) suggests supporting-context status rather than an independently-weighted category
matrix_row.conditional_offers: Yes in both tracks but structurally different — JUPAS's main mechanism runs on final HKDSE results rather than predictions (narrower pre-results conditional pathway exists via School Principal's Nomination, not fully verified this pass); non-JUPAS conditional offers based on predicted grades are the norm for IB/A-Level applicants applying ahead of final results
matrix_row.restricted_programmes: Layered capacity constraints: a system-wide ~15,000 UGC-funded local-place ceiling (protected, not reduced by non-local growth) plus a separate non-local quota (40% of local student number as of 2024/25, rising to 50% from 2026-27, additional and self-funded) plus programme-specific hard ceilings within both (Medicine most concretely documented — CUHK: 300 HKDSE-track + 25 advanced-standing places from 2025 entry)
matrix_row.turkiye_meb_direct_entry_complexity: Moderate: direct entry is possible only via non-JUPAS (JUPAS is categorically closed to Turkish applicants), and the university-specific minimum average for the same named Turkish diploma types genuinely differs — HKU: 4/5 or 70/100; CUHK: 80%; HKUST's specific figure unconfirmed. No Hong Kong-specific bridge/foundation-year mechanism or supplementary-qualification pathway (comparable to the Netherlands' AP-exam or Lisans-credit routes) was identified for shortfall cases.
matrix_row.dominant_counselor_risk: Assuming JUPAS is Hong Kong's UCAS — i.e., that because a national platform exists, it must be the route (or at least a viable route) for an internationally-educated Turkish/foreign-qualification applicant. It categorically is not: JUPAS is local-HKDSE-only, and every non-local applicant, regardless of any HKDSE result they might hold, must use each university's own separate non-JUPAS system. This is a more severe version of RULE-ADMISSIONS-012's 'platform existence does not imply centralized decision-making' — here the platform does not even ACCEPT this applicant type, rather than merely not deciding for them.

unresolved_questions: HKUST's specific published minimum-grade threshold for Turkish Lise-type diplomas (Anadolu Lisesi / Devlet Lise Diplomasi / Lise Bitirme Diplomasi) — not found in sources reviewed this pass, despite Turkey being confirmed as a listed/accepted country.

Whether holding IB/A-Levels alongside Turkish secondary schooling shifts a Hong Kong university's evaluation from the Turkish-diploma table to the IB/A-Level table, as it demonstrably does in the Netherlands — plausible by structural pattern, not independently confirmed for Hong Kong.
Any role (or confirmed non-role) of Turkey's YKS national university entrance exam in a Hong Kong university's assessment of a Lise diploma holder — no source reviewed addressed this either way.
